newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT - Bradesco rating raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Bradesco rating raised.

text.p: -- Bear, Stearns said in a report that it has raised its rating from leading Brazilian private bank Bradesco to attractive from neutral.
-- "In our view, the market has oversold the stock on recent unfavorable results reporting and this presents investors with an opportunity to accumulate shares," the brokerage said in a report.
-- Bear, Stearns said the stock's valuation of 1.3x is the lowest in the last 10 months.

-- Bradesco's price has fallen 15 percent since the bank reported its third-quarter 1996 earnings, the results of the weak figures and fears of monetary tightening by the Brazilian government, the brokerage said.
-- "Our analysis suggests that the decline in earnings was caused by a non-recurring increase in non-operating expenses and that the core banking business is performing extremely well," it added.
-- Bear, Stearns also said fears of a looming monetary tightening have been exaggerated, especially since the Central Bank on December 19 cut its base interest rates.
-- The bank's stock is now trading at a discount to banks Itau and Unibanco, its main competitors, it said.
-- The brokerage cited as positive a possible ADR listing by the bank, continued core operating strength, industrial portfolio, and its large capital base.
-- It said Brazil's macroeconomic picture and the lingering possibility of a monetary tightening are risks.
-- Bradesco preferred ended Monday at 7.55 reais while its voting common closed at 7.10 reais on the Sao Paulo bourse. The market was closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
